title: Sign of the permutation induced on deleted finite indices
statement: Let n be a natural number, sigma a permutation of Fin(n+1), and k in Fin(n+1). There exists a permutation tau of Fin(n) such that sigma(k.succAbove(a)) = (sigma(k)).succAbove(tau(a)) for every a, and (-1)^(sigma(k)) sign(tau) = sign(sigma) (-1)^k as integers.

source.place: Omitted verification of differential stability, expanded using Mathlib.GroupTheory.Perm.Fin and Mathlib.GroupTheory.Perm.Option

proof.text: Form pi by moving k to zero before applying sigma, then moving sigma(k) to zero. It fixes zero. Transport with finSuccEquiv and use Equiv.removeNone to construct tau; map_equiv_removeNone identifies tau.optionCongr with the transported pi. Fin.cycleRange_symm_succ and cycleRange_succAbove give the face identity.

Equiv.optionCongr_sign and Equiv.Perm.sign_permCongr identify sign(tau) with sign(pi). Apply sign_trans, sign_symm and Fin.sign_cycleRange to compute sign(pi). Multiply by (-1)^(sigma(k)); its square is one. This also covers n=0.

from.place: Deleted-index permutation and sign step of the signed-face proof

lean.statement:
theorem signed_face_permutation (n : ℕ) (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin (n + 1)))
    (k : Fin (n + 1)) :
    ∃ τ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n),
      (∀ a, σ (k.succAbove a) = (σ k).succAbove (τ a)) ∧
      (-1 : ℤ) ^ (σ k).val * (Equiv.Perm.sign τ : ℤ) =
        (Equiv.Perm.sign σ : ℤ) * (-1 : ℤ) ^ k.val
